official.deadline_note: The Ministry states each applicant is obliged to fill in the electronic application form by 30 September 2026 at the latest. The application register lists the call as 1 August to 30 September 2026, while the Ministry describes the application period as 21 August to 30 September 2026; the closing date is 30 September 2026 in both. Supporting documentation requested by the embassy follows a later date.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 academic year; electronic application form due 30 September 2026, studies starting in the 2027/2028 academic year
official.status_note: The 2027/2028 call ran from 21 August to 30 September 2026 and closed before the verification date; the following annual call had not been announced on the Ministry's page.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'Tuition fees are paid on behalf of the scholarship holders by the Government of the Czech Republic.'
benefits: Standard period of full-time study in an accredited programme at a Czech public university
Monthly scholarship: 16 000 CZK for students in follow-up master's degree programmes and 24 960 CZK for students in doctoral degree programmes
Tuition fees paid on behalf of the scholarship holder by the Government of the Czech Republic
Access to student dormitory accommodation and student canteen meals
Health care provided by the Ministry of Health to the same extent as for Czech insured persons
For the Czech-language route, a one-year preparatory Czech language course delivered by the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies, Charles University, forming part of the scholarship
eligibility: Citizen of one of the states listed in the 2027/2028 call: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine, Belarus (democratic opposition), Ethiopia, Gabon, Mauritania, Zambia, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Palestine, Guatemala, Honduras
Nationals applying for English-medium study may come from any of the eligible countries; the Czech-language route is offered only to citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine and Belarus
Not a citizen of the Czech Republic or of the European Union, and not another foreign national holding a permanent residence permit in the Czech Republic
Not enrolled at a university in the Czech Republic at the time of submitting the application
For follow-up master's study: completion of a bachelor's study programme; for doctoral study: completion of a master's study programme
Age limit for this call: date of birth after 1 September 1991 and before 31 August 2008
For English-medium study: sit the online entrance English language test during the application; for Czech-language study: Czech at CEFR B2 level exempts the applicant from the preparatory course
requirements: Fill in the electronic application form on the Ministry's portal by 30 September at the latest
Complete the compulsory online tests: the general academic prerequisites test, and additionally the English language test for English-medium study
The application is only accepted and evaluated once both compulsory tests are completed
Register only once and submit only one application
Attend the interview at the Czech embassy responsible for the country whose citizens were offered scholarships, and submit the requested documentation
documents: Documents relating to any studies started, completed or not completed
Overview of study and research stays abroad over the last five years (year, duration, location, purpose)
Motivation letter, maximum one A4 page for follow-up master's programmes and two A4 pages for doctoral programmes
Academic CV focused on studies and employment
Statutory declaration of return to the country of origin after completion of studies
Declaration of acceptance of the conditions for providing scholarships and of the conditions for the provision of health services

Officially certified copy of a foreign diploma, diploma supplement or transcript of completed subjects and exams, plus confirmation that the awarding institution was authorised to provide higher education
For doctoral applicants: an outline of the professional issues to be focused on and the idea of the dissertation focus
Letters of recommendation from professors at academic institutions (optional but requested in the application form)
selection_criteria: Files pass through the applicant's Czech embassy, then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT, which proposes the successful candidates
The most successful candidates are invited to submit complete documentation by the embassy deadline
There is no legal entitlement to the award of a scholarship
Applicants are proposed for the study programmes selected in the application; the award covers the standard duration of full-time study
coverage: The scholarship is intended to cover the essential costs of living and studying in the Czech Republic
Tuition fees are paid on behalf of the scholarship holder by the Government of the Czech Republic
Accommodation, meals and public transport are covered by the scholarship holder from the scholarship, under the same conditions as those applicable to Czech citizens
The MEYS does not reimburse travel expenses
The scholarship is usually paid by the host university in monthly instalments, commencing only after the holder's arrival and admission to study at the faculty
application_method: Prepare the required documents (passport, study documents, list of stays abroad, motivation letter, academic CV)
Set up a personal email account, which is used to log in to the registration system
Register on the Ministry's portal and complete the electronic application form, proceeding chronologically through applicant details, application information, documents and tests
Complete the compulsory tests within the application deadline
Respond to the Czech embassy's invitation and submit the requested documentation
official.application_route: Complete the electronic application form and compulsory online tests on the Ministry's portal by 30 September, then go through the Czech embassy for the interview and documentation.
official.citizenship_residency: Open only to nationals of the listed developing and specific third countries; Czech citizens, EU citizens and foreign nationals with permanent residence in the Czech Republic are excluded
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme exists specifically for foreign nationals from the listed partner states
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Study is restricted to the selected follow-up master's programmes offered in English or the selected areas offered in Czech, and to selected doctoral programmes offered in English, all published by the Ministry
official.research_requirement: For doctoral programmes, an outline of the professional issues on which the applicant intends to focus and the idea of the dissertation focus must be provided
official.duration: Standard duration of full-time study: two-year follow-up master's programmes (preceded by a one-year Czech language course on the Czech-language route), or three- to four-year doctoral programmes
official.description: The Government of the Czech Republic offers scholarships within the framework of its Foreign Development Cooperation in support of the study of foreign nationals from developing countries at public institutions of higher education in the Czech Republic, governed by Government Resolution No. 870 of 27 November 2024 and implemented jointly by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in cooperation with the Ministry of Health.
official.program_type: Government bilateral scholarship under the Czech foreign development cooperation programme
official.english_requirement: An applicant for a government scholarship in support of English-medium studies is obliged to sit an online entrance English language test in the course of the application submission, which proves that he or she has a sufficient command of English.

not_confirmed: the exact monthly amount applicable to any individual award beyond the two published levels - the Ministry and the application register publish 16 000 CZK for follow-up master's programmes and 24 960 CZK for doctoral programmes, and the recorded figure is the master's level
the embassy documentation deadline for the 2027/2028 round, which had not been published on the pages read
the start date of the next annual call after the 2027/2028 round
verification.notes: Amounts, tuition payment, travel non-reimbursement, age limits, eligible countries, tests and documents were read on the Ministry's own page and on the DAMS application register detail page for the English-language programme; the 2027/2028 call closed on 30 September 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: Read the published Guidelines PDF before you touch the form - the Ministry makes it binding, and it carries the conditions that decide admissibility. The gate that trips most applicants is the compulsory online tests: the application is not accepted or evaluated until both the general academic prerequisites test and, for English-medium study, the English test are complete, and they must be finished by the same 30 September cut-off. Money is tight by design - roughly 16 000 CZK a month for a master's student must cover dormitory accommodation, canteen meals and public transport out of the same pot, and travel to Czechia is never reimbursed.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Nationals of the listed partner states who have completed a bachelor's (for master's) or master's (for doctoral) degree, fall inside the 1991-2008 birth window, and can commit to the standard length of full-time study at a Czech public university.
application_readiness_checklist: Download and read the binding Guidelines for Granting Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic (2026) from the Ministry's page before starting the form
Check your country appears in the 2027/2028 list and that you are not already enrolled at a Czech university, which disqualifies you outright
Check your date of birth against the published window (after 1 September 1991 and before 31 August 2008)
Choose between the English route (open to all eligible countries) and the Czech route (only Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine, Belarus) before you plan your year
Book the English test and the general academic prerequisites test early in the window so a failed attempt still leaves time to retake before 30 September
Get certified copies of your diploma, diploma supplement and transcripts plus proof that your institution was authorised to award higher education
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the form but never completing both compulsory tests, which leaves the application unprocessed
Being a Czech or EU citizen, or holding permanent residence in the Czech Republic - an absolute bar with no appeals route
Missing the bachelor's degree for a master's application or the master's degree for a doctoral application
Falling outside the published age window for the call
Choosing the Czech-language route without B2 Czech, which forces the extra preparatory year
Assuming travel to Czechia is funded - the Ministry states plainly that travel expenses are not reimbursed
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to and from Czechia, and anything beyond dormitory, canteen and public-transport costs - the 16 000 CZK monthly allowance has to absorb those, and installation or relocation support is not offered.
document_audit: Diplomas and supplements must be officially certified copies, not plain photocopies, and must be accompanied by confirmation that the awarding institution was authorised to provide higher education
The motivation letter is length-capped at one A4 page for master's applicants and two for doctoral applicants - going over reads as not following instructions
The statutory declaration of return to the country of origin after completing studies is mandatory and must be signed
The list of study and research stays abroad must cover exactly the last five years with year, duration, location and purpose
Doctoral applicants additionally need an outline of the professional focus and the dissertation idea
alerts: The call closes on 30 September and the next one is not announced until roughly August of the following year, so a missed round costs a full year
Each applicant may register only once and submit only one application - there is no second file
The Ministry describes the period as opening 21 August while the application register records 1 August, so treat late August as the safe assumption and do not wait for the later date
There is no legal claim to the award and no right of appeal, so embassy-stage documentation quality is decisive
Scholarship payments start only after you arrive and are admitted at the faculty - plan for the gap before the first instalment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the Ministry's portal, complete the electronic form with all documents attached, finish both compulsory tests before 30 September, then pass through the Czech embassy interview and documentation route to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT for the final decision.
